source.title: Exploring Grokking: Experimental and Mechanistic Investigations
source.authors: Qi-Ye Hu; Z. Hao; Ruo-Xi Yu

record.file_problem: The full text is present. The paper has an inconsistent venue/date signal: the supplied metadata says arXiv.org, 2024, while the text includes a NeurIPS 2022 footer.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own gradient-training results on modular-addition classification, an algorithmic task outside the claim versions’ specified settings.
record.gate_note: The study tests modular addition with p = 97, not CIFAR benchmarks or the mechanisms named in V2–V6. Its discussion of other papers’ findings is not recorded as this study’s result.
record.test_reason: The study reports modular-addition training and generalization in Transformers, MLPs and LSTMs. These results do not test the convolutional CIFAR setting of V1 or the specific comparisons and mechanisms in V2–V6. Changing learning rates alone does not test V5 without measuring stability thresholds or curvature.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors observe grokking in their Transformer experiments and conventional generalization in their tested MLP and LSTM configurations. They report that MLP training accuracy remained below 100% after 20,000 steps. These conclusions concern the tested configurations, rather than an architectural impossibility of grokking in MLPs or LSTMs.
record.recipe_differences: Modular-addition classification with Transformer, MLP, and LSTM models; it does not use the CIFAR benchmark recipes or interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-data fraction, model family, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, weight decay, and noise are varied in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: At a 30% training fraction, the modular-addition Transformer reached 100% training accuracy after about 200 steps. The tested MLP did not reach exactly 100% after 20,000 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested modular-addition Transformer quickly fits its training set perfectly; the tested MLP remains below perfect training accuracy at the reported budget.

fits_no_version.finding: The Figure 5 caption reports training accuracy achieved after approximately 100–200 updates across optimizer variants and training fractions, without explicitly specifying the accuracy level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested modular-addition Transformer attains its reported training-accuracy outcome early across the compared optimization settings.

record.peer_reviewed: The supplied text includes “36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022)” but the metadata identifies the source as arXiv.org; peer-review status cannot be determined from the text.
record.problems: The reported training-accuracy outcomes are for modular addition, not the benchmark settings in the claim. Some plotted outcomes lack numerical values in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric training-error outcomes stated in text were identified. Other plotted accuracy and loss curves are figure-only and do not provide extractable numeric values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels and size, stopping and regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts and the specified initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions; R1 still records a clear observed training-accuracy result outside their scope. Section 5 summarizes other studies and supplies no additional original test of these versions.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and varying student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth, batch normalization, and the cited special-initialization or Fixup conditions.
Initialization comparisons and signal or gradient propagation across network depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature or sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet, and Fixup comparisons.
